label: Diagram 2.3
caption: Diagram 2.3 | Minimum door and hall widths and restrictions on localised obstructions
description:
This diagram, titled "Minimum door and hall widths and restrictions on localised obstructions," depicts several floor plan arrangements showing door openings and hallway widths. 

The drawing contains four main scenarios. The first shows a door with a clear opening width of 775mm leading into a hallway 900mm wide. A second scenario shows a door with an 800mm opening leading into a hallway 1050mm wide. In this area, a 300mm nib is shown with a dotted line, and a 1500mm length of hallway is indicated. 

A third scenario illustrates a door with a 750mm opening and a hallway 1200mm wide, with a 1500mm length marked. A fourth section shows an 800mm door opening into a 900mm wide hallway. A 300mm nib is indicated with a dotted line, and a 750mm door leaf is shown. 

The key specifies that a shaded area indicates where a "Localised obstruction not permitted in shaded zone," while a dashed box indicates a "Permitted obstruction." A note states "Note 1: 300mm nib only required where door opens inward (shown dotted)." Another note states "*all dimensions are minimum except where noted."
